_readme: THE COMMAND LINES A CREDENTIALS PROFILE CAN BE MADE OF, shipped with the
product. It is data: add an engine, or correct one, without recompiling.
A profile is a home directory the engine is started with. Where a variable
moves that directory the switch costs a variable and nothing else; where
none does, the fallback is a symlink on the credentials file, which is more
fragile and is marked as such. `home` carries `variable` or
`credential_symlink`; absent means NO KNOWN WAY, which is not the same as
«nobody looked» — `home_note` says which, and it is read by a person.
`mark` is the two letters a crowded strip shows for this engine. Absent
means the first two letters of `id`, upper-cased.
`executable` is what actually reads that home, and it is the honest link: a
step naming a binary is matched on this and never on `id`, so a wrapper
does not get handed somebody else's credentials.
`already_at` is where that engine keeps its home when nothing moves it,
below $HOME. It is what `profiles adopt` takes as a profile: the
credentials already on the machine, read where they are and never copied —
a rotating refresh token held in two homes breaks both. Absent means
nobody established it, and `adopt` then asks for the directory by name.
`native` says whether the engine keeps profiles of its own: `supported`,
`not supported`, or `unverified`. A word this list does not know is read as
`unverified`, never as a no: a measurement invented from a misspelling is
worse than an admitted gap.
`endpoint` names the two variables that send the engine to an endpoint
other than its maker's, and the protocol that endpoint must speak. A
profile declaring an endpoint of another protocol is refused: nothing of
Sailor's translates in between.
`reads_instructions_from` lists the files the engine reads at its start,
each relative to the project root or under `~`. It is how a person learns
whether the engine can see the page of memories: `sailor memory where`
looks for the page's path inside those files. Absent means nobody
established what the engine reads — never `nothing`. An entry that is not
a list of such paths is refused with the engine's name, as is any other
field this list does not know.
To change the list on one machine, write $SAILOR_HOME/command-lines.json:
an `id` present there replaces the one shipped here, and ids not in here
are added.
`signed_in_when` names the files inside a home whose presence means somebody
signed in there. Measured on this machine, never guessed. Absent means NOBODY
ESTABLISHED IT, and no engine is ever refused for that: unknown is not signed
out. gemini and antigravity keep nothing under such a name, so neither declares one.
`signed_in_keychain` is the login keychain item that means the same where a
command line keeps its credentials there instead: `service`, a dash, and the
first `home_digest_chars` hex characters of the SHA-256 of the home's path.
Measured for claude on macOS, where a signed-in home has no credentials file.
`identity.file` lists candidate paths, relative to the home, that say
WHICH ACCOUNT that home answers as — read off the disk, never asked of the
engine, because the file is what a launch actually reads. They are tried in
order and the first one that actually carries the account wins, so a stale
file left behind by another home shape does not stop the search: an engine
that keeps the file beside its home rather than inside it, for its own
default directory, is a second candidate here, not a rule the code knows
by name. Absent means nobody
measured it yet for that engine: `identity_of_home` then answers «cannot
tell», never «matches». Measured for claude in `.claude.json`, inside a
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` home and beside the default `~/.claude` directory,
under `oauthAccount.emailAddress`.

command_lines.native_note: checked on 2.1.247: `auth` offers only login, logout and status, and `--help` names no profile or multi-account subcommand.
command_lines.home_note: checked against the installed binary: the variable moves the whole directory, credentials and settings included.

command_lines.native_note: `-p/--profile` layers `<home>/<name>.config.toml` over the base configuration: config profiles, not separate credentials.
command_lines.home_note: checked with `doctor`: it shows auth.json and config.toml inside the directory the variable names.

command_lines.native_note: no `--profile` in `--help`: only sessions (`--resume`, `--session-id`), not separate identities.
command_lines.home_note: checked against the installed source: the base directory is that variable, or `.gemini` under $HOME.

command_lines.native_note: `--help` and its subcommands name no profile option; nothing else was measured.
command_lines.home_note: its data lives under the Gemini CLI's directory, and GEMINI_CLI_HOME does NOT move it: the string is absent from the binary and the home follows $HOME. Two profiles of it therefore start in the same place, silently. That is measured, not unlooked-at.
